newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT sees huge losses on intl rate cut.
newsitem.headline: PLDT sees huge losses on intl rate cut.

text.p: The Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) said on Tuesday it expected to lose two billion pesos this year if international rates were cut and government failed to approve its proposed new rate plan.
The plan involves a rate increase for basic phone charges and a call metering scheme that will compensate for the reduction in accounting rates.
Accounting rates refer to the cost shared by a Philippine firm with its foreign counterpart carrier for every minute of international long distance calls, now at $1.0 per minute.

Based on documents submitted by PLDT to the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC), PLDT said it would face a two billion peso loss if accounting rates were reduced by 10 percent to $0.90 a minute without the new rate scheme in place.
On the accounting rate, PLDT has been negotiating with AT&T for a new rate.
PLDT pricing division head Miguela Villanueva said at a public hearing at the NTC that AT&T had "formally communicated" a $0.70 rate from the existing $1.0 per minute.
The companies, however, have yet to reach an agreement.
